newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Jan 25 Initial Claims from 351,000; Jan 25 4-Week Average from 344,750; and Jan 18 Continued Claims from 2,448,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 347,000 in the February 1 week.
The department said the four-week moving average for initial claims for the February 1 week was the lowest since the week ended November 9, 1996, when it stood at 330,500.
The department said 30 states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended January 25, the latest period for which data are available.
The largest were North Carolina, with 11,210; California, with 9,051; Pennsylvania, with 8,850; and Tennessee, with 8,158.
North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in various industries including textile, apparel and electrical equipment. California had fewer layoffs in the service industry.
Labor said one state reported an increase in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the January 25 week.
Texas, with 4,925 more claims, reported layoffs in the non-electrical machinery industry.
